title: Knight Ranking Parade
statement:
You are given an array A of N distinct integers representing the power levels of N knights standing in a row.

A knight at index i is called special if the number of knights with a greater power level on its left is strictly greater than the number of knights with a greater power level on its right.

Your task is to determine the total number of special knights.

Definition:
For each knight at index i:
- Left Count = Number of knights to the left of index i whose power is greater than A[i].
- Right Count = Number of knights to the right of index i whose power is greater than A[i].

The knight is special if:
  Left Count > Right Count

Input Format:
- input1: An integer N, representing the number of knights.
- input2: An integer array A of size N, representing the power levels of the knights.

Output Format:
- Print a single integer representing the number of special knights.

examples.explanation:
Knight 4: Left=0, Right=1 -> No
Knight 3: Left=1, Right=1 -> No
Knight 5: Left=0, Right=0 -> No
Knight 2: Left=3, Right=0 -> Yes
Knight 1: Left=4, Right=0 -> Yes
Total special knights = 2.
For every knight, Left Count is 0 while Right Count is equal to the number of larger elements to the right. No knight satisfies Left > Right. Total = 0.

Knight 5: Left=0, Right=0 -> No
Knight 4: Left=1, Right=0 -> Yes
Knight 3: Left=2, Right=0 -> Yes
Knight 2: Left=3, Right=0 -> Yes
Knight 1: Left=4, Right=0 -> Yes
Total special knights = 4.

constraints: All elements in A are distinct.
hints: Since all elements in A are distinct, total elements greater than A[i] is fixed: TotalGreater = N - Rank(A[i]).
If you know LeftGreater (number of elements to the left of i greater than A[i]), then RightGreater = TotalGreater - LeftGreater.
Use a Fenwick Tree (Binary Indexed Tree) or Segment Tree after coordinate compression to count LeftGreater in O(N log N) time.
discussion: Coordinate compression with Fenwick Tree to count strictly greater elements on the left in O(N log N) time and O(N) space.
